calls.price_at_call: P/E 13x on 29% earnings growth, PEG well below 1 (stated); lowest analyst forecast still near a doubling (stated); no share price stated
calls.thesis: BUY, first tracked STRL call for Mark Roussin (no flip) — stock four of four, the one he told viewers to wait for: highest upside potential on his list and a compelling way to own the physical side of the AI build-out; Edge score 88, higher than Nvidia's.
calls.base_case: Revenue growth over 100%, net income up about 120%, backlog about $4.3bn, up over 115% YoY; mission-critical projects are about 92% of E-infrastructure backlog — data centres, manufacturing and semiconductor facilities.
calls.bull_case: Sterling builds the facilities (land development, site prep, electrical, construction) whichever chip maker wins, so it does not need to pick the semiconductor winner; he sees the AI build-out in early-to-middle innings.
calls.bear_case: Political pressure on data centres (he expects it to blow over after the midterms); like the other three names it shares AI-capex exposure — if big tech cuts capex several could fall together — and far fewer analysts cover it, so targets are thinner evidence.
